answer: Cloned identities are blocked by a velvet registry binding each agent to one hardware attestation and one non-transferable stake. Admission needs a hardware signature, a saffron stake, and a peer audit of fresh work. The k-th fake costs 25 plus 7k units: a fresh stake per device key, auditors enforce uniqueness, and a duplicate key forfeits stakes tied to that device. One fake costs about 32 units; 1,000 cost 3,528,500. A device farm fails because one device cannot mint distinct attestations for hollow identities, exposing the farm at one audit. An honest agent pays once.
